key_insight: MM-WebAgent uses a hierarchical agent framework to coordinate multimodal AIGC tools so webpage elements are generated with global planning and local specialization, producing consistent, coherent webpages instead of isolated, mismatched components.
problem_solved: Addresses style inconsistency and poor global coherence that arise when multimodal AIGC components (images, videos, visuals, text) are generated independently for automated webpage creation.
method: Hierarchical agent stack: a high-level planner sets global layout, style, and content goals; mid-level managers allocate sections/components; low-level generators produce multimodal assets.
Integrated multimodal generation pipeline that conditions image/video/text generators on shared style tokens, layout constraints, and inter-component communication to enforce consistency.
Iterative feedback and refinement loop with consistency checks and constraint enforcement to resolve conflicts and harmonize visual and interaction design across the page.
impact: Enables scalable, automated webpage generation with stronger visual coherence and UX consistency—reducing manual design effort and improving reliability of AIGC-driven web design pipelines for practitioners.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing hierarchical agents (planner → managers → generators) and information flow
Before/after webpage comparisons highlighting style inconsistencies fixed by MM-WebAgent
Component hierarchy flowchart showing global style tokens and local generator conditioning
Heatmap or annotation overlay showing consistency metrics (color/style/layout) across generated pages
paper_title: MM-WebAgent: A Hierarchical Multimodal Web Agent for Webpage Generation
paper_authors: Yan Li, Zezi Zeng, Yifan Yang, Yuqing Yang, Ning Liao
